blogs.title: Aseptic Meningitis with a Normal MRI: Unmasking Acute Neuro‑Behçet’s Disease
blogs.description: When a CT and MRI show no focal lesions, CNS inflammation can still be the culprit. This post dissects how an older man with fever, headache, mucocutaneous ulceration and hyponatraemia was correctly diagnosed with acute neuro‑Behçet’s disease based on CSF lymphocytic pleocytosis and the classic mucocutaneous findings, guiding clinicians through the differential of infection versus inflammation when imaging is unremarkable.

blogs.title: SIADH in Neuro‑Behçet’s: The Silent Contributor to Hyponatraemia and Complications
blogs.description: CNS inflammation can provoke inappropriate ADH release, yet SIADH is rarely highlighted in Behçet’s. We examine the IL‑6‑driven mechanism of ADH over‑secretion, provide clinical pearls to recognize hyponatraemia (e.g., hiccups, unexplained rhabdomyolysis), and discuss fluid restriction, hypertonic saline and vasopressin antagonists in the context of concurrent diabetes.

blogs.title: Colchicine Versus Steroids: A New Paradigm in Acute Neuro‑Behçet’s Management?
blogs.description: Despite conventional steroid guidance, this case achieved full remission using colchicine alone. The article reviews colchicine’s anti‑inflammatory pathways, draws on current literature, and outlines strategies to consider colchicine as first‑line therapy when steroids are contraindicated or undesirable.

blogs.title: Cutting the Diagnostic Red Tape: Targeted Testing in Systemic Inflammatory Disorders
blogs.description: An extensive work‑up often adds little diagnostic value. We present a pragmatic algorithm for evaluating fever, headache and hyponatraemia, scrutinising the utility of serum ACE, soluble IL‑2R, HLA‑B51 and other serologies versus focused testing that directly informs a Behçet’s diagnosis.

blogs.title: From Hiccups to Hyponatraemia: Minor Symptoms Unmasking Major Electrolyte Disturbances
blogs.description: Persistent hiccups and early rhabdomyolysis, though seemingly unrelated, can signal severe hyponatraemia. This post explains the pathophysiology, outlines quick‑recognition cues for emergency providers, and offers evidence‑based monitoring and correction strategies to prevent neurologic sequelae.

blogs.title: Integrated Care of Diabetes and Behçet’s: Balancing Glycaemic Control Amidst Autoimmunity
blogs.description: Poor glycaemic control can aggravate infection risk and inflammatory disease activity. This article integrates diabetes management with acute Behçet’s care, illustrating how to adjust antidiabetic therapy during systemic flare‑ups while maintaining metabolic stability and preventing further complications.
